description: **A guide's orientation may be computed, and reading it as text refuses it.** Every guide property accepts a `{"signal": …}`, and the enum-valued ones were the last to notice: an object is not a word, so reading one as text produced `[object Object]`, the parse of it failed, and what happened next depended on the property. A legend's orientation fell back to its default corner with a diagnostic. An **axis's** took the whole axis with it — `return null` — so a chart lost the side of itself it reserves room along, and the surface came out 210 wide where upstream draws 241. That is not a style: an orientation decides which edge of the plotting area a guide is measured against, so a chart that moves its axis from left to right is a different layout and not a different colour, and a dashboard offering "labels on the left or the right" writes exactly this. Three properties are here because three were found: the axis's `orient`, the legend's `orient`, and the legend's `direction`, which decides whether entries run down or across — probed, a legend whose direction is a signal reading `horizontal` makes a 206-wide surface where the default vertical makes 172. Each is written as an **expression** rather than a bare name so the answer cannot be confused with a literal that happened to parse.
